correctness.rationale: The time-dependent secant-slope difference system is exact for two arbitrary distinct solutions. After removing the common decay and applying positive coordinate scaling, its continuous polar lift advances at a rate between 0 and sqrt(AB); consecutive zeros of the first coordinate require at least a pi angle increment. Strict monotonicity makes the departure direction nonzero. The logistic smooth-dependence proof has a simple linearized zero exactly at 4pi, establishing sharpness as a limit of genuine finite-amplitude returns. In the bounded monotone C1 endpoint example, the explicit decaying sinusoid remains inside the affine region for all t and yields identical first-coordinate records at k*pi for all prescribed nonzero amplitudes. The 129-point numerical code check is supplementary, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The new object is the minimum separation between first-coordinate intersections of any two trajectories of a natural negative-feedback planar flow. Its exact sharp threshold gives a uniform, nonlinear disconjugacy law and a guaranteed two-observation separation window using only regulation slope bounds. The bounded-feedback endpoint shows that exact loss of an entire sampled coordinate record can occur at the boundary despite strict monotonicity and global asymptotic convergence. This natural qualitative invariant is neither an arbitrary parameter slice nor an algorithmic recasting of derivative observability.
